subject: agriculture
intro: Agriculture leads to the science and business of feeding people — crop and soil research, livestock science, farm machinery, and the running of farms and ranches themselves.

roles.title: Soil and Plant Scientists
roles.what: Research crop breeding, physiology, yield and pest control, and study the composition of soils as it relates to plant growth — classifying and mapping soils and testing alternative field practices.
roles.where: Soil (unit 2) — formation, fertility, erosion and conservation — and principles of plant growth (unit 3), extended by the soil-health and plant-nutrition-and-fertilisers lessons, are the daily subject matter.

roles.title: Animal Scientists
roles.what: Conduct research into the genetics, nutrition, reproduction, growth and development of domestic farm animals, improving livestock health and productivity.
roles.where: Livestock units 6 and 7 — ruminant digestion, reproduction, nutrition and health — plus monohybrid inheritance and selective breeding (unit 9) are precisely the research questions this career pursues.

roles.title: Food Scientists and Technologists
roles.what: Use chemistry and microbiology to study food processing and deterioration, analyse nutritional content, and find the best ways to process, package, preserve, store and distribute food safely.
roles.where: Crop production and protection (units 4 and 5) and the food-systems-and-security lesson connect harvest quality, storage and pests to the preservation and food-safety work this career does.

roles.title: Agricultural Engineers
roles.what: Apply engineering technology and biological science to agricultural problems — farm power and machinery, structures, electrification, irrigation, soil and water conservation and crop processing.
roles.where: Drainage and irrigation (topic 2.5), land preparation (4.1) and the precision-agriculture lesson link the syllabus to the machinery, structures and water systems agricultural engineers design.

roles.title: Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers
roles.what: Plan and run farms, ranches, greenhouses and nurseries — supervising planting, cultivating and harvesting while handling the finances, marketing and hired labour of the operation.
roles.where: Principles of agricultural economics (topic 1.2) and the farm-economics lesson, with crop production, pasture management and livestock units, are the operating manual for this career.
